question: Can native N/C support improve the active geometric path under a mixture intervention on weights? Prior rounds on L109 varied only dose.native_rms_ratio (0.33, 0.66, 0.99) with weights fixed at half=1.0, endpoint=0, orientation=0, type=0; mean_pic50 rose monotonically (7.683, 7.784, 7.826) while joint_formation stayed low (0.25, 0.208, 0.208) and retention_after_formation was 1.0 with zero typed-fraction change. The proposed mixture values (half=0.95/type=0.05 and half=0.7/type=0.3) have never been tested at any dose, so no prior outcome at these exact weights exists. I need native_retention_evidence to check whether the native N/C boundary probabilities (C ~0.94-0.998, N ~0.88-0.95) reflect genuine local chemical support or only a generic decoder channel, and whether the low joint_formation is a formation deficit rather than a retention deficit. Falsifier: if native retention evidence shows the N/C boundary support is not locally compatible (e.g., no coordinate-space role for the target slots), then adding a type weight cannot improve the active geometric path and the mixture hypothesis fails. Smallest discriminating test: run the half=0.7/type=0.3 mixture at the already-tested native_rms_ratio=0.99 and compare joint_formation and mean_pic50 against the R03 half=1.0/type=0.0 baseline.
